messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging — Streaming decode p99 spike observed in us-west-2. Affected pools: decode-*-pool. p95 up ~2.3x, p99 up ~5.8x. Alert fired at 2026-03-12T09:02:03Z.
olivia (oncall): I'm on it. Noticed the spike lines up with the kernel rollout that completed ~2m ago (kernel v2.3.2) and the TRT/FlashAttention variant rollout.
jamie (eng-runtime): Confirmed on our side. Telemetry shows tail decode time increases during KV eviction churn. Stack traces reference the new compilepath kernels.
rishi (eng-sre): Any error increase or just latency? Customer impact?
kate (cs): CS reported three customers seeing streaming stalls — sessions remain open, but tokens stall for several seconds. No 5xxs.
leo (eng-infra): We can divert traffic to the legacy kernel pool to reduce exposure. Preparing the split.
jamie (eng-runtime): Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) divert 20-40% traffic to legacy kernel pool; 2) disable the `-Xemit-kv-evict` compile flag temporarily; 3) pin FlashAttention/TRT to stable variants.
jamie (eng-runtime): Mitigation commands below:
```bash
# split traffic (example)
redwoodctl traffic-split --pool decode-v2.3=70 --pool decode-legacy=30
# rollback kernel on a pool
deployctl rollback kernel --pool decode-v2.3 --to v2.2.8
# flip runtime flag
runtime-config set --name compile_emit_kv_evict --value false
```
deploy-bot: Acknowledged. Traffic-split job queued (job id: job-8821).
maya (eng-ml): FYI the TRT8 variant we rolled has a known tail-case under KV churn on sequence lengths > 2048 — pinning FlashAttention to v1.4 helped in staging.
olivia (oncall): Executing traffic-split now (running redwoodctl...).
deploy-bot: traffic-split started (job id: job-8821).
jamie (eng-runtime): After initial 30% split, p95 dropped ~28% and p99 improved ~40% for most shards, but two shards still show elevated tail.
leo (eng-infra): Rolling kernel rollback to v2.2.8 on the affected pool now. ETA ~3m.
deploy-bot: rollback in progress (job id: job-8830). Draining and replacing nodes.
jamie (eng-runtime): Monitoring — metrics trending down. Streaming stall count reduced by ~60% overall. Remaining two shards likely suffer from a hot KV-eviction path.
rishi (eng-sre): I'll cordon those two nodes and collect perf samples and kernel traces (perf + eBPF).
kate (cs): I'll send proactive customer comms now: "We're investigating intermittent streaming latency. We've applied mitigations and will update in 30 minutes."
jamie (eng-runtime): Rollback complete per deploy-bot. Observability shows p99 back near baseline for ~85% of traffic. Still tracking the two shards.
rishi (eng-sre): Collected flame graphs and kernel profiles uploaded to the ticket. Early signal points to a new code path in compilepath causing increased CPU stall during cache eviction.
maya (eng-ml): I'll add a targeted perf harness to reproduce under KV churn and long sequences; will link test artifacts to the ticket.
jamie (eng-runtime): Created follow-up: <https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFR-1234|INFR-1234> — assigned to eng-runtime/kernel-team. Marking P1 and adding logs/traces.
olivia (oncall): Notifying ops rotation and handing off for post-mitigation monitoring. On-call handoff in 30m. Who owns the postmortem/runbook?
jamie (eng-runtime): I'll own the runbook + postmortem. Will collect traces, perf tests, and recommend: revert compile flag, pin FlashAttention, and add a rollout canary for compilepath changes.
rishi (eng-sre): I'll schedule a follow-up action to add a live SLO dashboard for early detection of KV-evict correlated tail events.
kate (cs): Sent customer note and logged replies. Will update if customers escalate.
olivia (oncall): Closing acute mitigation loop here — traffic split + rollback completed, customer comms sent. Keeping thread open for the kernel-team investigation. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
